steps.title: Open UniProt home page
steps.instruction: Open a current web browser and navigate to http://www.uniprot.org.

steps.title: Select UniProt dataset
steps.instruction: Click the drop‑down panel to the left of the search box, view all UniProt datasets, and choose the dataset of interest (the panel background colour changes to indicate the selected dataset).

steps.title: Perform simple search
steps.instruction: Enter a query in the search box and click the Search button; for example, keep the default “UniProtKB” dataset and type “human insulin”. (Full UniProt query syntax is listed in Table 1 of the source.)

steps.title: Review search results view
steps.instruction: On the results page, choose either the “card” or “table” format using the icons at the top of the page (Figure 2 shows the table view).

steps.title: Apply result filters
steps.instruction: Click filters on the left side to narrow results: select “Human” under “Popular organisms”, then under “Proteins with” choose the filter “3D structure” (Figure 3).

steps.title: Open protein entry
steps.instruction: Click an accession link in the “Entry” column (e.g., INS_HUMAN (P01308)) to view the protein entry; the summary shows protein name, status, organism, gene name, length, evidence level, and annotation score, with tabs “Entry”, “Feature viewer”, “Publications”, “External links”, and “History”. Use the buttons below the summary to launch tools, download formats, add to basket, add a publication, or give feedback. If isoforms exist, align sequences; explore function, subcellular location, disease, variants, etc., via the navigation panel on the left. Further guidance is in the Guidelines for Understanding Results section.

steps.title: Open advanced‑search help
steps.instruction: Click the blue “Help” icon at the top‑right corner or the green “Help” icon on the right‑hand side of any page, then search for “advanced search” to view the advanced‑search options page that lists the menu items for UniProtKB.

steps.title: Start advanced search
steps.instruction: From the drop‑down menu left of the search box, confirm the dataset (default is UniProtKB). Then click the “Advanced” button to the right of the search box.

steps.title: Build advanced query
steps.instruction: In the advanced‑search panel, use the drop‑down boxes to select field types or type a concept name (e.g., “structure”) and pick the suggested term. Click the “Add field” icon to add rows, combine rows with Boolean operators “And”, “Or”, or “Not”, and finally click the Search button. Example: select field type “Organism” → enter “Homo sapiens”; next row select field type “Protein name” → enter “insulin”. (Figure 6 shows the panel.)

steps.title: Review advanced results
steps.instruction: Examine the search‑results page, where the selected parameters appear as active filters (Figure 7). Click accession links in the “Entry” column to view individual protein entries.

steps.title: Start keyword‑based advanced search
steps.instruction: Return to the UniProt home page, select “UniProtKB” from the left drop‑down, and click “Advanced”.

steps.title: Add Keywords field
steps.instruction: In the advanced‑search panel, click the drop‑down in a row, choose “Keywords”, and type “direct protein sequencing” (or select it from the autocomplete list). All keywords are listed at http://www.uniprot.org/keywords.

steps.title: Add Sequence/Encoded‑in field
steps.instruction: In the next row, click the drop‑down and select “Sequence/Encoded in”, then choose “Mitochondrion” from the suggestions.

steps.title: Add Function/Function [CC] field
steps.instruction: If needed, click the “Add Field” button at the bottom to create another row, select “Function/Function [CC]” from the drop‑down, then open the “Evidence” drop‑down on the right and choose “Experimental” under “Manual Assertions”. Leave the input field empty to include all values. Verify the layout matches Figure 8, then click the Search button.

steps.title: Examine keyword search results
steps.instruction: View the results page, which (as of December 2022) shows five matching entries (Figure 9). Click an entry accession to explore the protein entry in detail.
